newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG UNDERMINE TITLE CHANCES BY LOSING AT LE HAVRE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG UNDERMINE TITLE CHANCES BY LOSING AT LE HAVRE.

text.p: Paris St Germain undermined their title chances by slumping to a 1-0 defeat at lowly Le Havre in the French soccer league on Friday.
The Paris club were lucky to see Teddy Bertin miss a penalty after a foul by goalkeeper Bernard Lama on Le Havre striker Roger Boli three minutes from halftime.
But with 14 minutes remaining, another offence on Boli, this time by midfielder Benoit Cauet, gave Bertin another chance from the penalty spot.
Cauet scored from the spot to give victory to the Normandy club, who are fighting to avoid relegation.

Troubled Paris St Germain, who had shown signs of recovery by beating Lyon 3-1 to record their first win at Parc des Princes for four months last Sunday, are second seven points behind leaders Monaco.

Sylvain Legwinski scored twice to help Monaco win 3-0 at Rennes on Thursday to warm up for Tuesday's UEFA Cup quarter-final second leg clash with England's Newcastle. Monaco won 1-0 at St James' Park in the first leg.
Strasbourg moved up one place to third by winning 1-0 at former Eurpean champions Marseille thanks to a Pascal Nouma goal in the 51st minute.
Bastia, who could manage only a 2-2 draw with Montpellier in an eventful match in Corsica, dropped from third to fourth.
Christophe Sanchez put the visitors in front in the 16th minute but Bastia equalised through Patrick Moreau a minute later and added a second thanks to Sebastien Perez 10 minutes later.
But a goal by Jean-Christophe Rouviere in the next minute allowed Montpellier to share the points.
Nantes extended their unbeaten run to 22 matches by winning 2-1 away to bottom club Nice.

Chad striker Japhet N'Doram gave Nantes the lead after three minutes and Frederic Da Rocha made it 2-0 in the 76th minute. James Debbah scored a consolation goal for Nice with three minutes remaining.
Nantes, recovering from a poor start to the season, moved up one place to fifth in the 20-strong table.
"The good results we have obtained recently are starting to pay off," Nantes trainer Jean-Claude Suaudeau said. "Now we're beginning to think about a place in Europe next season."
Champions Auxerre boosted their morale ahead of a tricky European Cup quarter-final second leg against Germany's Borussia Dortmund on Wednesday by beating Cannes 3-1.
Goals by international midfielder Sabri Lamouchi in the 35th minute and striker Lilian Laslandes two minutes later gave Auxerre a 2-0 lead at halftime.
Liberian Victor Konwlo restored hope for Cannes with a goal in the 76th minute but Laslandes put the issue beyond doubt with his seond goal of the night three minutes from time.
"We hoped for a good result but Dortmund is not Cannes," Laslandes said, remembering that Auxerre lost 3-1 in Germany in the first leg. "It will be tough but we'll do our best."
